## Primary answer
**Predicted P(efficacy PR | Age = 65) ≈ 0.395 (≈ 39.5 %)** — fraction 0.3952, 95 % CI 0.262–0.529.

## Model actually fitted (statsmodels `Logit`, MLE, intercept, raw years, Age only)
logit P(PR) = **β̂₀ = 4.44657 (SE 1.45133)** + **β̂₁ = −0.0749539 (SE 0.0243505)** × Age
- OR per year of age = 0.9278; Age 95 % CI −0.1227 … −0.0272; p(Age) = 0.0021
- n = 80, **41 PR events vs 39 non-events (SD 17 + PD 22)**; unconditional PR rate 0.5125
- llf −50.0710, llf(null) −55.4268, LR-test p = 0.00106, McFadden pseudo-R² = 0.0966, AIC 104.14, converged = True

## Prediction trace at Age = 65
linear predictor = 4.446565 + (−0.074954)(65) = **−0.425439** → expit(·) = **0.3952** (39.52 %)
- delta-method SE 0.0678 → 95 % CI **0.2624 – 0.5280**
- profile-likelihood 95 % CI **0.2679 – 0.5287** (agrees with Wald)
- statsmodels `get_prediction` cross-check: p 0.3952, SE 0.0678, CI 0.2727 – 0.5325
- manual IRLS/Newton re-fit reproduces β̂ to 8.9e-16 (sklearn is not installed in this offline runner, so the MLE was verified by hand-Newton instead of an sklearn cross-check)
- standardised-Age refit gives the identical p(65) (diff < 1e-9), confirming scaling invariance

## Cleaning / data checks executed in the script
- raw read 121×12 → dropped rows with NaN `Sequence number` (41 blank rows incl. the last row holding only whitespace `" "` in `Age`) → **n = 80**, Sequence 1…80 contiguous, 0 duplicates
- `Age` numeric cast: **0 missing**, min **40**, max **75**, mean 58.54 (SD 10.46); **exactly-65 count = 5** (1 PR, 4 non-PR)
- `Efficacy` levels exactly {PR 41, PD 22, SD 17}; no whitespace/case variants

## Diagnostics (reported, not used to change the estimate)
mean fitted 0.5125 = observed 0.5125; predicted range 0.236–0.810; ROC AUC 0.701; Hosmer–Lemeshow χ²(3) = 0.31 (p = 0.96) → no miscalibration signal. Empirical reference at age 65: 1/5 = 0.20 (n = 5, too small to be a usable estimate — the model-based 0.395 is the answer).

## Sensitivity: SD handling (as agreed, secondary)
- **SD excluded, PR vs PD only (n = 63):** logit = 5.329 − 0.0801·Age → p(65) = **0.5306** (95 % CI 0.373–0.688); **Δ = +0.135 vs primary**. Primary retains SD as non-PR.
- **Group-1-only subset (n = 41, all PR):** outcome constant → complete separation, model not identifiable; documented as note, no coefficients reported (per your instruction).

## Limitations
`Groups` (treatment arm) is perfectly associated with PR (Group 1 = 41/41 PR; Group 2 = 0 PR), so an age-only model absorbs the treatment effect into the age slope — Age is a proxy/marker here, not causal (Group 1 mean age 54.9 vs Group 2 62.4). Interpret 0.395 as a fitted association in this 80-patient sample; the wide CI (0.26–0.53) reflects that.
